title: Normalizer conjugacy of Borel subgroups through a maximal torus
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; a maximal torus is one not properly contained in another torus subgroup. A group is solvable if its successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups eventually become trivial. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Let $G$ be smooth and connected, $T\subseteq G$ a maximal torus, and $B_1,B_2\subseteq G$ Borel subgroups containing $T$. Then there exists $n\in G(k)$ such that $nTn^{-1}=T$ and $nB_1n^{-1}=B_2$ as subgroup schemes. For a subgroup $J$, the conjugate $nJn^{-1}$ has $A$-points $n_AJ(A)n_A^{-1}$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, where $n_A$ is the scalar extension of $n$.

source.place: Corollary 17.11, final assertion, printed p.355; Theorems 17.9(b) and 17.10, printed pp.354--355.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to $B_1\subseteq G$, obtaining a separated finite-type quotient $p:G\to X$, faithfully flat and of finite presentation, with $p(a)=p(b)$ precisely when $a^{-1}b\in B_1$. As $B_1$ is smooth, connected and maximal smooth connected solvable, [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] makes $X$ proper. It is nonempty since $p(1)\in X(k)$. This quotient is canonically the represented fppf coset sheaf of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]: the map $G/B_1\to X$ is locally surjective because $p$ is an fppf cover, and injective because its fibres are exactly the right $B_1$-cosets. The functor of points of the scheme $X$ is a sheaf for fppf coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], since a flat, surjective, quasi-compact morphism is a one-member fpqc covering. Thus sheafification identifies the two quotients, compatibly with the maps from $G$. In particular every $x\in X(k)$ lifts to $g\in G(k)$. Left multiplication defines the action on $X$: for $u\in G(T)$ and $x\in X(T)$, the lifting clause of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] gives an fpqc covering $\{T_a\to T\}$ and $v_a\in G(T_a)$ with $x|_{T_a}=p(v_a)$; set $u\cdot x|_{T_a}=p(u v_a)$. Two lifts of the same section differ, by the coset criterion, by right multiplication by a section $b$ of $B_1$, and replacing $v$ by $vb$ does not change $p(uv)$; so these local sections agree on the overlaps $T_a\times_TT_b$ and glue uniquely to a section of $X(T)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], naturally in $T$. This gives a morphism $G\times X\to X$ with the action identities, since those identities are the multiplication identities on local representatives.

source.place: Theorem 17.9(b), proof, p.354; Definitions 5.20 and Theorems 5.28, 7.18, pp.104--105,142.

proof.text: Restrict this action to $B_2$. The group $B_2$ is smooth, connected and solvable, and $X$ is nonempty, proper and of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$. By [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point], choose an $x\in X(k)$ fixed scheme-theoretically by $B_2$, and lift it to $g\in G(k)$ as in step 1. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $b\in B_2(A)$, fixedness gives $p_A(bg_A)=p_A(g_A)$. The coset-fibre criterion of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient], with $a=g_A$ and $b$ there equal to $bg_A$, gives $g_A^{-1}bg_A\in B_1(A)$. Hence $B_2\subseteq gB_1g^{-1}$ as subgroup schemes. Conjugation by $g$ is an isomorphism with inverse conjugation by $g^{-1}$, so $gB_1g^{-1}$ is a smooth connected solvable closed subgroup: its commutator series is the conjugate of that of $B_1$. Maximality in the definition of $B_2$ now gives $gB_1g^{-1}=B_2$.

source.place: Theorem 17.9(b), proof, p.354, using Corollary 17.3, p.353.

proof.text: Put $S=gTg^{-1}$. Since $T\subseteq B_1$ and $T\subseteq B_2$, both $S$ and $T$ are torus subgroups of $B_2$. They are maximal there. Indeed, a torus in $B_2$ containing $T$ is a torus in $G$ and hence equals $T$. If a torus $R\subseteq B_2$ contains $S$, its inverse conjugate $g^{-1}Rg$ is a torus in $G$ containing $T$, so equals $T$, and $R=S$. Conjugation preserves the property of being a torus because it is an isomorphism of group schemes.

source.place: Corollary 17.11, proof, p.355: the two maximal tori in the conjugate subgroup.

proof.text: Apply the maximal-torus conjugacy clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] to the ambient group $B_2$, and to its maximal tori $S$ and $T$. Its hypotheses hold: $B_2$ is affine and of finite type by the standing hypotheses on all groups, and is smooth and connected by the Borel hypothesis. It yields $h\in B_2(k)$ with $hSh^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes. This invocation needs neither reductivity of $G$ nor reductivity of $B_2$.

source.place: Corollary 17.11, proof, p.355, applying Theorem 17.10 to the smooth connected group $B_2$.

proof.text: Set $n=hg\in G(k)$. On every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, associativity gives $n_AT(A)n_A^{-1}=h_Ag_AT(A)g_A^{-1}h_A^{-1}=T(A)$. Likewise $n_AB_1(A)n_A^{-1}=h_AB_2(A)h_A^{-1}=B_2(A)$. For the last equality, $h_A\in B_2(A)$ and conjugation by $h_A$ and by its inverse carry the subgroup $B_2(A)$ into itself. These equalities are natural in $A$, so are the required subgroup-scheme equalities $nTn^{-1}=T$ and $nB_1n^{-1}=B_2$.

source.place: Corollary 17.11, proof and final assertion, p.355: the element $hg$.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.9(b), p.354, and Corollary 17.11, proof and final assertion, p.355; maximal-torus conjugacy Theorem 17.10.

lean.statement: theorem torus_normalizer_borel_transitivity {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G T B₁ B₂ : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsAffine G.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] [Smooth G.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.X.left] (iT : T ⟶ G) (hT : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsMaximalTorus iT) (i₁ : B₁ ⟶ G) (hB₁ : IsBorelGroupScheme i₁.hom.hom) (i₂ : B₂ ⟶ G) (hB₂ : IsBorelGroupScheme i₂.hom.hom) (j₁ : T ⟶ B₁) (hj₁ : j₁ ≫ i₁ = iT) (j₂ : T ⟶ B₂) (hj₂ : j₂ ≫ i₂ = iT) : ∃ n : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G.X, ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Set.range (fun t : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ T.X ↦ (toUnit (StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A) ≫ n) * (t ≫ iT.hom.hom) * (toUnit (StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A) ≫ n)⁻¹) = Set.range (fun t : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ T.X ↦ t ≫ iT.hom.hom) ∧ Set.range (fun b : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ B₁.X ↦ (toUnit (StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A) ≫ n) * (b ≫ i₁.hom.hom) * (toUnit (StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A) ≫ n)⁻¹) = Set.range (fun b : StandardGroupSchemes.affine k A ⟶ B₂.X ↦ b ≫ i₂.hom.hom)
